A.name: Session-stateful inference provider for long-idle, long-context agents
A.one_line: A hosted open-model provider whose billable unit is a durable warm agent session: KV kept resident across minute-to-hour gaps via client-hinted HBM -> RAM -> NVMe demotion over unforked vLLM, billed as residency plus delta tokens, proven by a public idle-gap-resume benchmark against the strongest OSS offload baseline.
A.strongest_version: The physics is real and reproduced inside a production engine: at 16k a RAM-tier restore is 17x faster than cold prefill, and the only concurrent test of a purpose-built contiguous pinned-RAM connector held a 300-session load where the stock offload of that era collapsed. Agent workloads are ~120K-token prefixes with human gaps whose p90 is 20 minutes and a p99.9 turn over 45 minutes, and every provider's cache is a request-local LRU that cannot see session structure - the SGLang maintainers say so in their own RFC. The product makes the session the billable unit: a client-hinted, tier-spanning residency policy over unforked vLLM, verified-lossless resume, residency metering, and a public benchmark run against the strongest open-source offload baseline with raw logs. If IGR-1 shows the policy holds fewer GB-hours at equal p99, or holds p99 where stock offload degrades under burst, that is a measured operational advantage a generalized provider cannot get from a config flag. If it does not, six to seven weeks bought a benchmark, a modern connector, and a provider-TTL dataset the founder can sell, upstream, or fold into another direction.

B.one_line: A vLLM KVConnector plugin plus session gateway that pins voice sessions predicted to return soon and cheaply restores the rest, sold on a measured sessions-per-GPU at p95 TTFT <= 300 ms — today a single-seed 1.5x on an L40S/7B with an 8 ms margin, unmeasured against current stock offload tiers, on H100, or on production-size models.
B.strongest_version: A voice-session-aware residency layer that runs inside the buyer's own vLLM (later SGLang) as a plugin, sells a single measured number — concurrent sessions per GPU at full-load-window p95 TTFT <= 300 ms — and ships the harness and raw logs so buyers reproduce it on their GPUs and transcripts. Its one genuinely new mechanism is actuating a per-request idle-window prediction as HBM pinning through the stock KVConnector delayed-free hook, which is the only configuration of five that moved the measured knee (seed 1, L40S, 7B, 1.5x, 8 ms margin); the contiguous pinned-slab restore path that kept N=300 stable where a 2025 LMCache collapsed is the supporting substrate. The honest proof is a four-baseline benchmark (vanilla vLLM, vLLM's native OffloadingConnector, LMCache 0.5.x, SGLang HiCache) with a shuffled-hint ablation, 3 seeds, on H100 with a 26-35B model and partner transcripts; if predicted-idle pinning beats client-fixed TTLs and stock LRU tiers by >= 2x there, the sessions-per-GPU number becomes a line-priced capacity guarantee no voice or KV vendor in the research publishes. C.name: Session-aware serving engine: one residency scheduler for every idle regime (hosted + BYOC)
C.one_line: A hint-driven KV residency scheduler (pin / RAM / NVMe / drop per session) inside stock vLLM, sold hosted and BYOC, whose one in-engine win (voice arm D, 300 vs 200 sessions per L40S) is single-seed, synthetic-trace and 8 ms from failing, and whose agent-regime claim has no in-engine measurement above 16k tokens.
C.strongest_version: The strongest honest form is a benchmark-first BYOC product on stock vLLM: a session-aware connector plus an enforced residency policy and a published hint protocol, sold to voice and agent platforms that already self-host open models and pay by concurrency, with the vkv harness as the proof instrument they can run themselves. Its one measured advantage is narrow but real in-engine: on a 46 GB L40S with a 7B model, per-request return-time hints lifted the 300 ms-p95 ceiling from 200 to 300 synthetic sessions where vanilla vLLM, LMCache 0.3.2 and the same connector without hints all stopped at 200, and the physics underneath (pinned-RAM restore 10-17x faster than re-prefill single-request) is proven. Every shipping KV layer evicts by LRU-family policy and the hint RFCs that would change that are unimplemented, so the policy layer is genuinely unoccupied. The claim earns a public benchmark only after three seeds, a modern OffloadingConnector/LMCache 0.5.x baseline, FP8 KV and an H100 point, because each of those could erase an 8 ms margin; and the agent regime, where the larger customer and the session-hour pricing live, must first show that vLLM can restore 100K-token sessions in-engine at all, which neither repo has done. If both gates pass, the product is 'more sessions per GPU inside the SLA, with hits you can see'; if only the voice gate passes, it is a voice-serving optimization sold per GPU-hour.

H.strongest_version: The strongest honest form is a benchmark-first BYOC/hosted endpoint for screenshot agents whose pitch is verifiable per-step economics rather than a novel engine: an open VLM whose tokenizer bills 322 tokens for a 1280x800 frame against 1,105-1,334 on frontier tokenizers, served on stock vLLM with prefix caching, behind a gateway that reports observed (not modeled) per-step cost against the buyer's chosen baseline and keeps screenshots inside the customer's VPC. Its proof is a published $/completed-task page on a browser suite with five seeds, five backends and two screen sizes, where the 1280x800 arm openly shows parity with vanilla vLLM and the 1080p arm tests whether the visual-token cap holds grounding. If that gate passes, the defensible additions are session-affinity routing measured by cached_tokens across replicas and a re-keyed duplicate-frame cache, priced per step; if it fails, the product is a hosted/BYOC open-VLM endpoint with telemetry at roughly hosted-Qwen prices, which the founder may still choose to pursue. The delta-perception engine remains a separately gated R&D bet with a measured ~2.3x ceiling and an mRoPE blocker.
H.weeks_to_proof: 7-9 weeks to the first credible public proof (a $/completed-task and success page on WebArena or Odysseys with 5 seeds, 5 backends, 2 screen sizes, published trajectories and per-request usage). Assumptions: one engineer full-time; the existing gateway/backend/compose reused as-is with the len/4 estimator replaced by vLLM usage fields; ~60-100 GPU-hours for the suite runs (~$150-250 at Modal A100 $2.50/h) plus ~30 GPU-h for the multi-replica affinity test and ~20 GPU-h for A100/H100 throughput; a Sonnet 5 API arm (unmeasured spend, on the order of hundreds of dollars for 100-200 tasks x 5 seeds); browser/VM infrastructure for the suite; harness bring-up taking 1-2 weeks (the most likely slip); kill gate 1 (grounding at the capped budget) reviewed at week 2-3 before any affinity work. If OSWorld-Verified is chosen instead of a browser suite, add 1-2 weeks for desktop VM infrastructure and a desktop agent harness. No design partners exist, so pilot-derived proof is not in this window.

I.name: Fast Parse — the Morph playbook on document-to-structure (one specialized VLM plus a page-shaped engine)
I.one_line: A one-model inference company serving document-page-to-markdown/JSON on a purpose-built vLLM-based engine (copy speculator, visual-token budgeter, page scheduler) priced per page; the only in-repo evidence is a buyer-replicable resize lever on 200 short-answer pages, and every Morph-specific mechanism is unmeasured.
I.strongest_version: A per-page document-parse API built on an open 4B-8B VLM, where the company's proprietary work is (a) a task-trained draft head that exploits the copy-like structure of parse output, (b) a page-shaped engine with batch and latency lanes and a visual-token budgeter, and (c) a fine-tuned model evaluated on public benchmarks with a rerunnable harness — all sold in the unit buyers already use, against per-page list prices from $1.50 to $50 per 1,000 pages. The in-repo evidence supports only the economics precondition: an open 7B at 1024 px matched a 2024 frontier model on 200 short-answer pages at 2.7x its own higher-resolution throughput, in-engine, on an A100. Everything Morph-specific — copy fraction, copy speculation, the trained speculator, engine-level pruning, the fine-tune, full-page throughput under load — is unmeasured, and the first two weeks decide whether a well-configured vLLM already captures the gain. If gates 1-4 pass, the company has a measured engine advantage on a workload with public benchmarks, Apache-2.0 bases and a published data recipe, and can publish a proof buyers can rerun. If gates 2 and 4 fail, the honest fallback is a fine-tuned-model-plus-per-page-pricing company, which the founder must weigh against Reducto r-1, Mistral OCR 4 and the open OCR models as facts, not verdicts.
I.weeks_to_proof: 8-10 weeks to the first credible public proof of the engine claim (well-configured vLLM baseline vs engine v0 on full-page parse, olmOCR-Bench + DocVQA, 3 seeds, A100 + H100, public rerunnable harness), assuming 1-2 engineers, ~$3-5k of Modal GPU and frontier-API spend, that vLLM's speculative-decoding path accepts Qwen3-VL image inputs (unverified; not in the research files), and that the week-1 copy-fraction gate passes. 14-18 weeks if speculation must be built into the multimodal path (the week-2 slip risk) or if the fine-tuned model is part of the proof (~50k synthetic pages at ~$0.12 = ~$6k plus ~40 GPU-h, three weeks not one). The draft's 6 weeks assumed engine, fine-tune, load harness generalization, and three signed pilots with zero prior customer conversations in the repos.

J.name: Preemptible-GPU inference made safe by portable session state
J.one_line: Run long-lived agent sessions on spot GPUs by making per-session KV portable to a durable tier and restorable on any instance; value is conditional on an unmeasured fast-durable-tier bandwidth at the customer's real context size, with only identical continuation proven below that crossover.
J.strongest_version: The honest strong form of J is a kill-and-resume proof, not a spot pitch: a session-addressed inference endpoint on interruptible GPUs where every session's KV is continuously written through to a tier that survives the instance, and a SIGKILL on instance A is followed by the session's next step on instance B with published resume p95, GPU-seconds, identity, and resume-storm GB/s, benchmarked against the buyer's own fallback (vanilla vLLM re-prefilling the transcript) and against LMCache/OffloadingConnector object tiers. The repos already give it what no competitor's docs describe together: in-engine cross-instance bit-identical restore at TP=1, a working V1 connector skeleton with async load and an adaptive load-vs-recompute policy, a contiguous pinned-slab transfer pattern that held N=300 where LMCache 0.3.2 collapsed, and a session API/control-plane skeleton. Its economics are expressible only because portable KV turns a preemption into bytes divided by bandwidth, which lets a preemptible per-token tier carry a restore SLO instead of Morph-style admission gating. The entire direction rests on one number nobody has measured, per-request restore bandwidth from a fast durable tier into vLLM paged KV at 64k-128k, and one distribution nobody has collected, the real context sizes of self-hosted open-weight agent steps; a one-week tier gate and two design-partner histograms decide whether J is a product or a determinism feature on a session-affinity router.
J.weeks_to_proof: 8-10 weeks to a credible public kill-and-resume benchmark at TP=1 on Llama-3.1-8B (three seeds, 8k-128k ladder, baselines vanilla vLLM prefix caching / LMCache 0.5.x S3+NVMe / vLLM OffloadingConnector, per-point tier GB/s). Assumptions: 1-2 engineers full-time; ~$3-6k GPU spend at Modal/spot rates (~150-250 GPU-hours incl. reruns); an S3/remote-NVMe backend for the dexa SessionStore or LMCache's backends lands in week 1 and the tier gate (>=0.5 GB/s per request at 128k) passes; chunked-prefill save (vllm_connector.py:608) plus the port of the voice connector's block-keyed contiguous-transfer path and a rebase from vLLM 0.24.0/0.9.2 to 0.28.0 take 2-3 weeks; generalizing the voice harness (text prompts, aiohttp abort, server-metric scraping, provenance, multi-seed) takes 2 weeks; runs and write-up 2 weeks. The draft's 6-week figure assumed the tier backend, harness generalization and API rebase were free and included a design-partner pilot with partners that do not exist in the research files. Add 4-6 weeks if the proof must include the buyer's TP>1/MLA model class; the hosted spot fleet, registry, preemption handler and streaming gateway are beyond the benchmark and not costed here. The week-1 gate can end the effort at week 1.

If the 2026 OSS stacks hold N=300 out of the box, K still owns the standard, the certification and the retention policy; if an H100 dissolves the L40S wall, K still owns the measurement that proved it.
